summary: The packet socket a DHCP client reads its replies through, run as a process on Rach2 with an e1000 on QEMU's user network

cases.behavior: A packet socket refuses what it does not support, sends a DHCP discover whole and receives the broadcast offer that ip_rx drops, keeps ARP and IPv4 frames apart, is listed in /proc/net/packet while bound and not after its close, and is refused to an ordinary user

execution.privileges: root; a child drops to an ordinary user
execution.cleanup: nothing to remove; its sockets close at exit

assertions.checks: a stream packet socket is refused with ESOCKTNOSUPPORT
a packet socket for IPv6, which this stack has no frames for, is refused with EINVAL
a packet socket opens with no protocol, as arping opens it, and with IPv4's
PACKET_AUXDATA is refused with ENOPROTOOPT
a bind to an interface that does not exist is refused with ENODEV
a bind to the machine's interface is accepted
a DHCP discover sent to the broadcast MAC address is sent whole
a destination of four bytes, which is not a MAC address, is refused with EINVAL
poll reports the socket readable while the offer is awaited, and recvmsg then finds a frame
select, given a whole fd_set, agrees with poll
each frame received is at least an IP header long and IPv4
recvmsg reports no control data
recvmsg reports a sockaddr_ll naming this Ethernet interface, as a broadcast, with a sender
recvmsg reports no message flags
the offer is a BOOTP reply to 255.255.255.255, which ip_rx drops
a MSG_DONTWAIT receive on the emptied socket answers EAGAIN
the receive that failed leaves the caller's address and its length as they were
a second discover is sent, and its offer is read through recvfrom
recvfrom given 16 bytes for the address reports its true length, 20
the 16 bytes written are the start of this interface's sockaddr_ll
recvfrom writes nothing past the 16 bytes the caller declared
a bind naming ARP and a missing interface is refused with ENODEV, and getsockname still reports IPv4
a third discover is sent, and its offer is queued
a rebind to ARP is accepted and drops the offer queued under IPv4
a packet socket opens and binds to ARP
SIOCGIFHWADDR reports the interface's hardware address
getsockname on the ARP socket reports a whole sockaddr_ll of 20 bytes
getsockname reports the family, protocol and interface bound, an Ethernet hardware type and a 6-byte address
getsockname reports the address that SIOCGIFHWADDR gives
a second packet socket opens and binds to IPv4
the ARP socket sends an ARP request of the probe's own
the gateway answers a ping, whose reply is IPv4 traffic for the other socket
every frame the ARP socket receives is ARP
every frame the IPv4 socket receives is IPv4
the ARP socket receives a reply from the address the request asked about, and the IPv4 socket an IPv4 frame
/proc/net/arp has the gateway the machine resolved
four packet sockets in a row each open and bind after the one before closed
/proc/self/fd gives each socket's inode, and /proc/net/packet reads with Linux's heading
each bound socket has one row of /proc/net/packet, by its inode
after each close /proc/net/packet has no row of the socket closed
a child that drops to an ordinary user is refused a packet socket with EPERM, and exits normally

native.reason: the native machine's card is its own, not QEMU's e1000
